title.en: Interlocking burr and its disassembly order

summary: Design an interlocking puzzle whose only freedom at each step is a short list of legal slides, and expose that list.
objective: Build an invented six-piece interlocking puzzle where each state offers only the slides that are actually free, with an undoable disassembly history.
intent_signals: Design an interlocking wooden puzzle I can take apart step by step.
Show which piece is blocking the one I am trying to move.
example_prompts: Build a six-piece burr puzzle with legal slide detection and an undoable disassembly history.
Show the first free piece of an interlocking assembly and why the others are blocked.
negative_signals: Not a solved-puzzle catalogue reproduction; the piece set here is invented.
Not a physics assembly simulation with friction, tolerance or jamming.
not_for: Not a solved-puzzle catalogue reproduction; the piece set here is invented.
Not a physics assembly simulation with friction, tolerance or jamming.

entities.name: Notched pieces
entities.guidance: Author each piece as a stick with removed unit notches so the interlocking is real geometry that can be inspected off the assembly.

entities.name: Legal slide test
entities.guidance: Determine free directions per piece by cell occupancy along the slide axis and expose the blocking piece by name when a slide is refused.

entities.name: History spine
entities.guidance: Record each partial slide offset and each removal so reverse stepping restores exact model poses; the rack is a separate display-only inventory view.

state_contract.model: Voxel occupancy per piece on a shared lattice, a legal slide test along axis directions, and an ordered removal history. Motion is snapped along the lattice; no forces are involved.
state_contract.authority: Occupancy is authoritative. A slide is offered only when every cell along the path is free, so a piece never passes through another even mid-animation.
actions: Try to slide a selected piece along an axis.
Inspect the reported blocking piece when a slide is refused.
Remove a freed piece and continue.
Step the history backwards to reassemble.

invariants: A refused slide names at least one blocking piece rather than failing silently.

No model pieces overlap during legal slide animation; test the swept volume between lattice positions. Rack duplicates are explicitly display-only inventory views in a separate rack region, not additional model occupancy or physical transport.
The history stores every partial slide offset as well as removals, so stepping backwards reproduces the exact assembled state including pieces that were only partly withdrawn.
motion_guidance: Animate a slide along one axis at constant speed and stop it exactly at a lattice position.
When a piece becomes free, indicate the newly available slides rather than moving it automatically.
known_limits: Invented piece set: it is not a reproduction of any published burr and its difficulty is not calibrated.
Real wooden puzzles rely on tolerance and friction, which this lattice model deliberately ignores.

Before presenting the invented pieces as solvable, provide a verified disassembly sequence or a sound search that finds one under the axis-only rules. Budget exhaustion without a solution reports solvability not established, not no legal move. Report no permitted slide only after a complete current-state candidate legality test finds none; that local dead end is distinct from a global impossibility proof.
Authored guidance only: no scene runtime, rendering or numerical calibration has been run for this recipe.

object_craft.structure: Square-section sticks with unit notches, visible end grain and slight edge chamfers so the interlock reads at close range.
object_craft.material: Timber-like family with per-piece grain direction variation rather than colour coding, so the puzzle stays believable as an object.
object_craft.articulation: Pieces translate along a single axis at a time and are parented to the assembly frame otherwise.

object_craft.structure: A rack beside the puzzle holding removed pieces in removal order.
object_craft.material: Rack material subdued so attention stays on the puzzle; slot labels carry the step index.
object_craft.articulation: After a verified extraction clears the assembly, hide the assembly-view piece and show a display-only duplicate in its rack slot. No physical path to the rack is claimed. Undo removes the duplicate and restores the saved fully extracted pose before reversing recorded legal slides.

physical_contract.scope: Lattice-snapped sliding with occupancy tests; no friction, gravity or compliance.
checks: Occupancy never overlaps during or after a slide.
Reverse stepping restores the assembled configuration exactly.

creative_affordances: Vary the notch pattern to change difficulty; a single extra notch can make a different piece the first to free.
The rack, workbench and lighting are free design choices as long as the blocking report stays legible.
